reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to see the order list so I know which customers are in this batch and can check the handoff's refund claims.
The handoff claims refunds were applied to orders 102, 103, and 105. Before paying anyone, I'll check the refund ledger to confirm those refunds actually exist, since net_balance depends on them.
The refund ledger matches the handoff exactly: orders 102, 103, and 105 with the claimed amounts. Next I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
acme's net of 33983 matches my own check: orders 100 and 103 total 46215, less the 12232 refund on order 103. Next I'll get birch's balance.
birch's net of 65068 matches my own check: orders 101 and 104 total 65068 with no refunds. Next I'll get cobalt's balance, the last customer in the batch.
All three net balances match my own check against the orders and refund ledger: acme 33983, birch 65068, cobalt 2634. No problems found, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.
acme's payout is recorded. Next I'll record birch's payout of 65068, which matches the net_balance figure I already checked against the orders.

acme and birch are paid. Cobalt's net of 2634 matches my check: orders 102 and 105 total 38498, less refunds 2289 and 33575 (35864), leaves 2634. I'll record that payout, which is the last one in the batch.

All three payouts were recorded successfully. Each amount matches the net_balance figure and my independent check against the orders and refund ledger, and every order in the batch (100 through 105) was accounted for.
